Title: Effect of Neurolytic Celiac Plexus Block Guided by Computerized Tomography on Pancreatic Cancer Pain
Author: Chun-Lei Zhang et al.
Comment: Only the Day 14 endpoint was extracted; other follow-up times were excluded. The paper reports P < 0.01 but no exact p-value, t statistic, or degrees of freedom, so those numeric fields are null. M_diff was computed as control minus treatment: 2.9 - 2.0 = 0.9, so positive favors NCPB. SE_diff was computed from the reported SDs and randomized group sizes: sqrt(1.1^2/29 + 0.6^2/27) = 0.2346. Hedges g was computed from the reported endpoint means, SDs, and group sizes using the pooled SD and small-sample correction; it is oriented positive for lower pain with NCPB. The paper reports 29 and 27 patients randomized but does not explicitly provide day-14 analyzed Ns; these allocation Ns were used because no earlier attrition was reported, although 10 deaths occurred within 90 days.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group 1: single bilateral CT-guided neurolytic celiac plexus block with absolute alcohol, with rescue MS Contin if needed') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Medium: CT-guided interventional pain procedure versus oral pharmacological therapy
Topic of Content: Pain due to unresectable pancreatic cancer
Participant type: Patients with chronic upper-abdominal pain secondary to unresectable pancreatic cancer
Outcome measurement: Visual analogue scale pain rating at Day 14
